steps.prompt: New quest: read {quest} (and the v0 run, code and fixture screens it cites). Write the spec to {run}/spec.md following your role card, with numbered test cases and hand-checked expected values; every fixture screen in .crew/quests/crew-talk-v1/screens/ gets its own case (expected command text, kind, risky), plus the thinking/phantom screens that must be rejected. Include the who-touches-what table. Reply when it's written.

prompt.un-automate-monde: Spec: {run}/spec.md (quest: {quest}). Implement it in the source files the spec assigns the builder, and nothing else. Run .crew/gate.sh before replying.
prompt.le-testeur: Spec: {run}/spec.md (quest: {quest}). Write its test cases in the test file the spec assigns the tester, and nothing else. The builder is coding in parallel.

steps.prompt: Run the gate (.crew/gate.sh) and write the gate note to {run}/gate-note.md as your role card says.

Review the round's changes against {run}/spec.md and {quest}: git diff for edited files, and read the new files (git status lists them). This round changes code that can approve a crew member's shell command, so review it like security code: the bridge still decides risky; :unknown prompts are never allowable from the game; the new hold action uses the same token/exact-Origin/length checks and writes only state/hold.edn; a prompt is published only after two consecutive polls >= 2 s apart that both show a real permission block; nothing beyond names, states, the parsed prompt and log lines leaves a screen; the log never holds the token. Also: pure logic tested against every fixture screen; no member sent keys or prompts to the crew or started the bridge/watcher; names from the roster. Write the review to {run}/review.md.
